hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

paper.title: Decreased lipidated ApoE-receptor interactions confer protection against pathogenicity of ApoE and its lipid cargoes in lysosomes.

findings.finding_description: Cell-surface LDLR was immunostained after 1 d of treatment with lipidated ApoE isoforms in APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes, H4 and WT HAP1 cells. LipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, which the authors interpret as impaired LDLR recycling. The reported effect is shared by E3 and E4, with no E4-specific defect versus E3 described, so it does not support an APOE4>APOE3 recycling impairment. Directness 3 because surface LDLR is a surrogate for recycling and ARF6 was not examined.
findings.quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake (Figure 2A–D, Figure S2A–B).
findings.summary: LipApoE3 and lipApoE4 equally reduce surface LDLR versus lipApoE2 in human iAstrocytes, implying impaired recycling, but there is no E4 vs E3 difference.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes, H4 neuroglioma and HAP1 cells treated with exogenous POPC-lipidated ApoE2/E3/E4

findings.finding_description: In APOE KO iAstrocytes, all lipApoE isoforms upregulated LDLR mRNA. Only lipApoE3/E4 prevented the expected rise in surface LDLR, which the authors attribute to impaired recycling. Again E3 and E4 behaved alike.
findings.quote: While all 3 ApoE isoforms impacted LDLR mRNA levels, lipApoE3/E4 abrogated the expected increase in surface LDLR by impairing its recycling.
findings.summary: Despite LDLR mRNA upregulation, lipApoE3/E4 (not E2) prevent the rise in surface LDLR in astrocytes; E4 is no different from E3.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: Super-resolution imaging of APOE KO iAstrocytes showed internalized lipApoE fully colocalized with endogenous LDLR, largely inside LAMP1 compartments. The fraction of LAMP1 vesicles containing ApoE followed ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2 (Mander's coefficients 0.497, 0.410 and 0.266). This indicates LDLR is redirected toward lysosomes rather than recycled, with a modestly larger effect for E4 than E3; significance for E4 vs E3 was not stated.
findings.quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4) (Figure 2I).
findings.summary: In human astrocytes, ApoE–LDLR complexes accumulate in LAMP1 lysosomes in the order E4 > E3 > E2, consistent with LDLR diversion away from recycling.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes, super-resolution imaging

findings.finding_description: In H4 cells, cell-associated ApoE colocalized with LDLR puncta outside transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes. This suggests LDLR is trapped by ApoE in non-recycling endolysosomal compartments. The finding concerns the recycling route the hypothesis implicates (ARF6 itself was not studied) and was described for lipApoE3/E4 together.
findings.quote: Cell-associated ApoE immunoreactivity extensively colocalized with LDLR puncta (Figure 2G) outside of transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes (Figure S2D), suggesting “trapping” of LDLR by ApoE in other endolysosomal compartments.
findings.summary: ApoE–LDLR puncta sit outside transferrin-positive recycling endosomes, suggesting LDLR is trapped away from the recycling pathway.
findings.experimental_system: H4 human neuroglioma cells treated with lipApoE3/E4

findings.finding_description: In H4 cells, LDL uptake (DiI-LDL) served as a functional readout of surface LDLR availability. Co-treatment with lipApoE3/E4 inhibited DiI-LDL uptake by 60–65%, and 1 d pre-treatment nearly abolished it. LipApoE2 had no effect, or modestly enhanced uptake. E3 and E4 were similar.
findings.quote: When cells were co-treated with lipApoE and DiI-LDL for 3–4 h, both lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to 60–65% inhibition of DiI-LDL uptake, likely via a direct competition with LDL for LDLR binding, whereas lipApoE2 had no effect (Figure 2J, L).
findings.summary: LipApoE3/E4 (equally) suppress LDLR-mediated LDL uptake, a functional surrogate for depleted surface LDLR.

findings.finding_description: Total LDLR (surface plus intracellular) was immunostained in H4 cells. LipApoE3/E4 treatment produced a modest but significant reduction, with more clustered signal.
findings.quote: Immunostaining of total LDLR (cell surface + intracellular) in H4 cells after lipApoE3/E4 treatment showed a modest but significant reduction in signals, which also appeared slightly more clustered (Figure 2E–F).
findings.summary: LipApoE3/E4 modestly reduce and cluster total LDLR in H4 cells.

findings.finding_description: SPR showed lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 bind the LDLR extracellular domain with similarly high affinity (KD 9 nM vs 16 nM), while lipApoE2 binds about 50-fold more weakly. The near-equal E3/E4 receptor engagement is consistent with the absence of an E4-specific recycling defect. Directness 5 because this is cell-free binding, not receptor recycling.
findings.quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D).
findings.summary: LipApoE4 and lipApoE3 bind LDLR with similar affinity, unlike lipApoE2.
findings.experimental_system: Cell-free SPR with recombinant LDLR ECD and lipidated ApoE

findings.finding_description: In APOE KO iAstrocytes, pHrodo-lipApoE uptake followed the same isoform trend seen in other cells (E3/E4 > E2). The trend was abolished by blocking with LDLR ECD, showing LDLR-dependent endocytosis of ApoE in astrocytes. This reflects internalization only and is an upstream surrogate for receptor trafficking.
findings.quote: Lastly, in human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes (iAstrocytes), pHrodo-lipApoE uptake showed similar isoform trend that was abolished by blocking uptake of lipApoE3/E4 with LDLR ECD (Figure S1I–J), validating findings in a CNS cell type.
findings.summary: Astrocytes take up lipApoE3/E4 more than E2 via LDLR.

findings.finding_description: Cultured human cells were treated with exogenous lipidated ApoE3 or ApoE4. Both isoforms led to endolysosomal trapping of LDLR and depletion of cell-surface LDLR, with reduced LDL uptake. Only lipApoE2 lacked this effect, so no ApoE4-specific impairment relative to ApoE3 is reported, and ARF6 was not examined.
findings.quote: LDLR-mediated uptake of lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to endolysosomal trapping of LDLR and depletion of cell surface LDLR, resulting in further reduced LDL uptake. LipApoE2 did not show these effects due to defective LDLR binding.
findings.summary: LipApoE3 and lipApoE4 similarly cause LDLR endolysosomal trapping and surface loss, giving no ApoE4-over-ApoE3 recycling defect and no ARF6 data.
findings.experimental_system: human cell lines/iPSC-derived cells treated with recombinant lipidated ApoE isoforms (multiple human cellular models)
findings.data_location: Discussion (source figure not specified in this excerpt)

findings.finding_description: Across uptake assays with lipidated ApoE isoforms, ApoE4 was minimally differentiated from ApoE3. This argues against an ApoE4-specific defect in receptor-mediated endocytic trafficking compared with ApoE3 in these human cell models.
findings.quote: Although ApoE isoform-dependent receptor binding could only explain protective mechanism of ApoE2, with ApoE4 minimally differentiated from ApoE3 in most uptake assays
findings.summary: ApoE4 behaved much like ApoE3 in receptor-mediated uptake assays, which counts against an ApoE4-specific trafficking defect.
findings.experimental_system: human cell models (e.g., H4, HAP1, iPSC-derived astrocytes/microglia/neurons) treated with lipidated ApoE isoforms
findings.data_location: Discussion (source figures not specified in this excerpt)

findings.finding_description: Direct binding assays showed comparable LDLR-binding affinity for lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, and about a 50–100-fold lower affinity for ApoE2. These are cell-free binding data and only a weak surrogate for receptor recycling.
findings.quote: we demonstrated a ~50–100-fold decrease in LDLR-binding affinity for ApoE2 vs. ApoE3/E4 and a comparable binding affinity for ApoE3 and ApoE4.
findings.summary: ApoE3 and ApoE4 bind LDLR with comparable affinity.
findings.experimental_system: cell-free binding assays with recombinant lipidated ApoE and LDLR extracellular domain
findings.data_location: Discussion (source figure not specified in this excerpt)

findings.finding_description: Cells, including APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes, H4 and HAP1 cells, were treated with pHrodo-green-labeled lipidated ApoE isoforms. Uptake was imaged live at 5–6 h or 1 d. Across lipidation batches the trend was ApoE4 >= ApoE3 > ApoE2. This is a surrogate at both ends of the hypothesis: exogenous ApoE isoform protein is added rather than cell genotype being varied, and ligand endocytosis is measured rather than ARF6-related receptor recycling. If anything, it shows no impairment of ApoE4 internalization relative to ApoE3.
findings.quote: The exact uptake efficiency of ApoE4 vs. ApoE3 varies across different lipidation batches, but an overall trend of ApoE4 >= ApoE3 > ApoE2 was observed.
findings.summary: Lipidated ApoE4 is taken up at least as efficiently as ApoE3; recycling and ARF6 are not measured.
findings.experimental_system: H4 cells, HAP1 lines and APOE KO iPSC-derived human astrocytes treated with exogenous pHrodo-labeled lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: HAP1 cells were incubated for 1 d with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms and stained for cell-surface LDLR. The figure title states that lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, but not LDL, sequester LDLR, which implies reduced surface LDLR with both isoforms rather than an ApoE4-specific defect. Exact values and which comparisons were significant are not given in this excerpt. HAP1 is not a brain cell, and ARF6 was not examined.
findings.quote: Figure S2. Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, but not LDL, sequester LDLR, related to Figure 2 (A) Confocal images of cell surface LDLR staining for HAP1 cells after 1 d incubation with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE.
findings.summary: Both lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 reduce surface LDLR (sequestration) in HAP1 cells, so the defect is not shown to be ApoE4-specific.
findings.experimental_system: HAP1 human cell line treated with recombinant POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: H4 neuroglioma cells were treated for 1 d with lipidated ApoE4 and pulsed for 15 min with Alexa 488-transferrin to label recycling endosomes, then co-immunostained for ApoE and LDLR. This addresses where receptors localize relative to recycling endosomes. Only ApoE4 is described, with no ApoE3 comparator and no quantification, so the experiment does not test an APOE4-versus-APOE3 difference.
findings.quote: (D) Confocal images for co-immunostaining of ApoE and LDLR in H4 cells after 1 d treatment with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE4 followed by 15 min incubation with Alexa 488-labeled Transferrin to label recycling endosomes.
findings.summary: Imaging places LDLR and ApoE4 relative to transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes in H4 cells, but there is no ApoE3 comparison.
findings.experimental_system: H4 human neuroglioma cells treated with POPC-lipidated ApoE4

findings.finding_description: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes were treated for 1 d with lipidated ApoE isoforms, and 3 genes were quantified by qPCR, presumably as a check on whether the reduced surface LDLR reflects transcription. Neither the outcome nor statistics are given in this excerpt, and recycling was not measured directly.
findings.quote: (C) Relative expression of 3 genes quantified by qPCR for APOE KO iAstrocytes after 1 d treatment with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE (n = 3 independent experiments). Data shown are mean ± SEM.
findings.summary: qPCR of 3 genes in iAstrocytes after ApoE isoform treatment, with no statistics reported.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: Uptake of pHrodo-labeled lipidated ApoE isoforms into APOE KO iAstrocytes was measured, with or without LDLR extracellular domain as a competitor. This measures isoform-dependent endocytosis through LDLR, not receptor recycling or ARF6.
findings.quote: (I) Confocal images of pHrodo green-labeled POPC-lipidated ApoE (used at 10 μg/mL) detected in APOE KO iAstrocytes after 1 d incubation, with and without co-treatment of 20 μg/mL LDLR ECD.
findings.summary: ApoE isoform uptake into human iAstrocytes depends on LDLR, which bears only indirectly on receptor trafficking.
